ruling.recommended_action: Escalate to RydeHELP human review as a safety/conduct case: provide the reviewer the chat transcript (18:21 driver no-smoking request, 18:22 rider message), the keyword-flag metadata, and both profiles; advise the driver of the 995 / commercial-insurance / RydeHELP reporting paths; take no fare action.
ruling.escalation_reason: Threat of physical violence recorded in in-app chat (rider: “Say that again and I will punch you.” at 18:22, keyword “punch” auto-flagged) in response to the driver's no-smoking request; SAFE-1 requires human review instead of an automated ruling.

rejected_claims.reason: Correct insofar as profile facts cannot decide the case [F7][SAFE-1], but the claim that a clean record 'does not neutralize' the threat is not a determinable issue here — SAFE-1 routes the threat to human review regardless of profile, so the point is moot rather than adjudicated [F4][F5][SAFE-1].

Accepted as context only: the GPS record shows a normal trip (8.8 km vs 8.9 km optimal [F1]; 13.3 min vs 16 min [F2]), but these facts are irrelevant to the SAFE-1 trigger, which rests on the chat threat alone [F4][F5][SAFE-1].

The account-history point cannot support a finding of genuineness or of pattern: profile facts may not decide this case [F8][F7][SAFE-1], and no clause in the policy makes 427 trips / a 4.5 rating a basis for crediting the referral [F8][SAFE-1]. The rider's clean record likewise neither contradicts nor confirms the flagged message [F7][SAFE-1].

The driver's statement [F6] is consistent with the chat log [F4] but adds no independent corroboration; under the system-record-over-statement rule and SAFE-1's plain terms the escalation rests on the recorded, auto-flagged chat threat [F4][F5][SAFE-1], not on the statement.
